title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
summary: The translation of a system of particles or a rigid body is described by one point — the centre of mass (COM): treat all external force as acting at the COM, Ma_cm = F_ext. Internal forces don't change the motion of the COM.

Every linear quantity has a rotational partner: displacement → θ, velocity → ω, acceleration → α, mass → moment of inertia I, force → torque τ, momentum → angular momentum L. The formulas have the same shape: τ = Iα, L = Iω, KE = ½Iω².

Moment of inertia depends on mass and on how far it is from the axis (I = Σmr²). Learn I for standard bodies; for other axes use the parallel axis theorem (I = I_cm + Md²) and the perpendicular axis theorem (I_z = I_x + I_y, planar bodies only).

With zero external torque angular momentum is conserved (Iω constant) — a skater spins faster by pulling in her arms. In rolling without slipping v = ωR and KE = ½mv²(1 + k²/R²); on an incline the body with smaller k²/R² reaches the bottom first.

formulas.name: Centre of mass
formulas.formula: x_cm = Σmᵢxᵢ / Σmᵢ;   continuous: x_cm = ∫x dm / ∫dm;   r_cm = Σmᵢrᵢ / M
formulas.when: COM of particles or a body.
formulas.note: The COM can lie outside the body (ring, L-shape).

formulas.name: Standard centres of mass
formulas.formula: semicircular ring 2R/π;  semicircular disc 4R/3π;  solid hemisphere 3R/8;  hollow hemisphere R/2;  solid cone h/4 (from the base)
formulas.note: All distances are measured from the flat side / centre.

formulas.name: Motion of centre of mass
formulas.formula: M v_cm = Σ mᵢvᵢ (total momentum);   M a_cm = F_ext;   F_ext = 0 ⇒ v_cm constant
formulas.note: After an explosion the COM continues on the same parabola.

formulas.name: Rotational kinematics
formulas.formula: ω = ω₀ + αt;   θ = ω₀t + ½αt²;   ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ;   v = ωr, a_t = αr
formulas.note: θ in radians; multiply revolutions by 2π.

formulas.name: Torque
formulas.formula: τ = r × F;   |τ| = rF sin θ = F × (perpendicular distance)
formulas.note: A force through the axis gives no torque.

formulas.name: Newton's second law for rotation
formulas.note: Take I about the same axis as τ.

formulas.name: Angular momentum
formulas.formula: L = r × p;   rigid body: L = Iω;   τ = dL/dt
formulas.note: Even a particle moving in a straight line has L about a point (= mvr⊥).

formulas.name: Conservation of angular momentum
formulas.mistake: L is conserved but rotational KE is not (KE increases when arms are pulled in).

formulas.name: Moment of inertia and radius of gyration
formulas.formula: I = Σmr² = ∫r² dm;   I = Mk²  (k = radius of gyration)
formulas.note: I depends on the axis — 'I of a disc' is incomplete without the axis.

formulas.name: Standard moments of inertia
formulas.formula: ring (centre ⊥) MR²;  disc ½MR²;  hollow sphere ⅔MR²;  solid sphere ⅖MR²;  rod (centre ⊥) ML²/12;  rod (end) ML²/3;  ring (diameter) ½MR²;  disc (diameter) ¼MR²;  solid cylinder (axis) ½MR²

formulas.name: Parallel axis theorem
formulas.when: Parallel axis at distance d from the COM.
formulas.mistake: Always start from the axis through the COM, not any other axis.

formulas.name: Perpendicular axis theorem
formulas.mistake: Don't use it for 3-D bodies (sphere, cylinder).

formulas.name: Rotational KE, work and power
formulas.formula: K = ½Iω²;   W = ∫τ dθ;   P = τω
formulas.note: W = τθ only for constant torque.

formulas.name: Rolling without slipping
formulas.formula: v_cm = ωR;   K = ½mv²(1 + k²/R²);   incline: a = g sin θ/(1 + k²/R²);   v = √[2gh/(1 + k²/R²)]
formulas.note: The contact point has zero velocity; friction does no work (energy is conserved).

formulas.name: Which rolls down first
formulas.formula: k²/R²: solid sphere 2/5 < disc/solid cylinder 1/2 < hollow sphere 2/3 < ring 1 ⇒ solid sphere first, ring last
formulas.mistake: Mass and radius don't matter — only shape (k²/R²).

formulas.name: Equilibrium of a rigid body
formulas.formula: ΣF = 0 (translational) and Στ = 0 about any point (rotational);   couple: zero net force, torque F × d
formulas.note: Take torques about the point where unknown forces act — the equations get shorter.

examples.title: COM of two particles
examples.problem: 2 kg at x = 0 and 3 kg at x = 5 m. COM?
examples.solution: x_cm = (0 + 15)/5 = 3 m — closer to the heavier mass.

examples.title: Disc: centre and rim
examples.problem: Disc 2 kg, R = 0.5 m. I about the perpendicular axis through the centre and a parallel axis through the rim?
examples.solution: I_cm = ½MR² = 0.25 kg·m². At the rim: I = I_cm + MR² = 0.75 kg·m² (= 3/2 MR²).

examples.title: I of a rod about its end
examples.problem: 3 kg, 2 m rod, perpendicular axis through one end. I?

examples.title: Torque
examples.problem: A 10 N force acts 0.5 m from the nut on a spanner, at 30° to the spanner. Torque?

examples.title: Skater
examples.problem: A skater with I = 4 kg·m² spins at 3 rad/s and pulls in her arms to I = 2 kg·m². New ω and KE?
examples.solution: I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂ ⇒ ω₂ = 12/2 = 6 rad/s. KE goes from 18 J to 36 J — it increases (her muscles did work).

examples.title: Solid sphere on an incline
examples.problem: A solid sphere rolls without slipping down a 30° incline of height 7 m (g = 10). Acceleration and speed at the bottom?

examples.title: KE of a rolling disc
examples.problem: A 2 kg disc rolls at 4 m/s. Total KE?
examples.solution: K = ½mv²(1 + ½) = ½ × 2 × 16 × 1.5 = 24 J (one-third of it rotational).

examples.title: Flywheel
examples.problem: A flywheel starts from rest with α = 2 rad/s² for 5 s. ω and θ?
examples.solution: ω = αt = 10 rad/s. θ = ½αt² = 25 rad.

examples.title: Radius of gyration
examples.problem: k of a ring of radius 1 m about a diameter?
examples.solution: I = ½MR² = Mk² ⇒ k = R/√2 ≈ 0.71 m.

examples.title: Power of a motor
examples.problem: A motor delivers 20 N·m of torque at 50 rad/s. Power?

examples.title: Seesaw
examples.problem: A 30 kg child sits 2 m from the pivot. Where should a 40 kg child sit to balance?

topics.title: Rigid bodies and types of motion
topics.explain: In a rigid body distances between particles don't change. Motion can be pure translation (all points have the same velocity), pure rotation (about a fixed axis), or both (rolling).

topics.title: Centre of mass vs centre of gravity
topics.explain: The COM is set by mass distribution; in uniform g the centre of gravity is the same point. A symmetric uniform body has its COM at the geometric centre. A force applied at the COM causes only translation.

topics.title: Meaning of torque and angular momentum
topics.explain: Torque is the tendency to rotate — a door handle is far from the hinges for this reason. Angular momentum is the 'momentum' of rotation. For a particle, L = mvr⊥ about any point.

topics.title: What moment of inertia depends on
topics.explain: Mass, how the mass is distributed and the position of the axis. A ring has larger I than a disc of the same mass (all its mass is at the rim). Flywheels keep most mass at the rim for smooth rotation.

topics.title: Linear vs rotational analogy
topics.explain: x ↔ θ, v ↔ ω, a ↔ α, m ↔ I, F ↔ τ, p ↔ L, F = ma ↔ τ = Iα, KE ½mv² ↔ ½Iω², P = Fv ↔ τω. Remember one set and the other follows.

topics.title: Rolling motion
topics.explain: Rolling = translation + rotation. The top point moves at 2v, the contact point at zero. Static friction makes rolling possible but does no work. On a smooth incline a body only slides, it cannot roll.

topics.title: Examples of angular momentum conservation
topics.explain: A skater or dancer pulls in her arms — I decreases, ω increases. A diver curls up in the air to do more somersaults. A man on a rotating stool pulls dumbbells inward. Planets move faster near the Sun (Kepler's second law).

ratta: Ma_cm = F_ext;  internal forces don't move the COM.
τ = Iα;  L = Iω;  K = ½Iω²;  P = τω.
Ring MR², disc ½MR², solid sphere ⅖MR², hollow sphere ⅔MR², rod ML²/12 (centre), ML²/3 (end).
I = I_cm + Md²;  I_z = I_x + I_y (planar).
Rolling: v = ωR;  a = g sin θ/(1 + k²/R²).
Race: solid sphere > disc > hollow sphere > ring.
COM: semicircular ring 2R/π, disc 4R/3π, solid hemisphere 3R/8.
